provenance.source: National Energy Code of Canada for Buildings 2020, Division B, Subsection 8.4.4 — retrieved via the building-codes MCP server (necb:2020), Tables 8.4.4.7.-A/-B/8.4.4.13 and Articles 8.4.4.6-8.4.4.19
provenance.note: Rule values are transcriptions of the code text. Runtime never contacts the MCP server; regenerate/verify this file against the code text when editions change.
provenance.non_rule_keys_note: None: furnace_staging and dx_staging graduated to consumed rule blocks in D-46 (read by the efficiency pass's post-sizing staging pass), so the orphan-key exemption list is now empty.

selection.default_category_article: 8.4.4.7.(3): 'If the building or space type ... is not listed in Table 8.4.4.7.-A, the type that most closely corresponds to that thermal block shall be used'

rules.article: 8.4.4.7.-A: 'Where the proposed building or space has a cooling capacity exceeding 20 kW, the reference building or space shall use System 2'
8.4.4.7.-A: 'food preparation with kitchen hood or vented appliance -> System 4'

heated_only.text: Where the proposed building or space is heated only, the reference building or space shall use System 1.

compatible_cooling.text: Where ... heated as well as being cooled with an air-cooled unitary, packaged terminal or room air conditioner (or heat pumps), or fan coils, the reference ... shall be modeled as being identical to that of the proposed building or space

otherwise.text: otherwise, the reference building or space shall use through-the-wall systems.

heat_pump.text: Where the proposed ... includes an air-source, water-source or ground-source heat pump ..., the reference building's HVAC system for that thermal block shall be an air-source heat pump described in Table 8.4.4.13 (packaged unitary rooftop heat pump, CV, furnace + baseboards auxiliary). System 2 selections keep Table 8.4.4.7.-B.

purchased_heating.text: one gas-fired modulating boiler complying with Section 5.2. shall be used to represent the purchased energy equipment

oversizing.text: heating oversized by the lesser of (proposed %, 30%); cooling oversized by the lesser of (proposed %, 10%)

power_caps_w_per_kw.note: D-38 (A3 ruled min-wins, phylroy 2026-07-28): the reference must also MEET Part 5 prescriptive (8.4.4.1.(2)) - after the pump-power transfer, each hydronic loop's COMBINED pump motor power is clamped at these W per kW of the loop's peak thermal demand at design. Values verified against the printed 2020 AND 2025 tables via MCP (identical).

hydronic_pumps.transfer: sentences (1)-(3) via one mechanism: combined peak W/(L/s) by plant-loop type from the sized proposed model ((2) combined by summing power AND flow); reference pump rated power = intensity x its own sized flow
hydronic_pumps.sentence_5: variable-flow pumps are modeled as a pump riding its curve -> riding-curve coefficients on every reference PumpVariableSpeed
hydronic_pumps.floor_note: below-D floor (P = E x Prated) approximated by the minimum-flow clamp at D x rated flow; polynomial at D equals E within table rounding (0.691 vs 0.68, 0.043 vs 0.04)

hx.modeling_note: frost_control/threshold_temperature_c/defrost fractions are EnergyPlus equipment-modeling assumptions (E+ defaults; -23.3 C = -10 F), NOT NECB values — 5.2.10.1 is silent on frost control. Sentence (5) test-method certification and the sentence (3) specialized-exhaust exemption are modeller/equipment scope.

energy_recovery.text: Where Subsection 5.2.10. applies to a reference building HVAC system, that system shall be modeled with energy recovery capabilities that comply with Subsection 5.2.10.; energy recovered from exhaust air shall be used to preheat the outside air supplied by that system.
energy_recovery.trigger_provenance: NECB 2020 Tables 5.2.10.1.-A (p.147, non-continuous) / -B (p.148, continuous), verified identical in 2025; retrieved via codes MCP get_table 2026-07-22. Replaces the NECB 2011 150 kW exhaust-heat-content trigger previously implemented here (wrong vintage — divergent for small high-%OA systems, where 2020 requires and 2011 does not).
energy_recovery.effectiveness_article: 5.2.10.1.(4) — >= 50% ENTHALPY effectiveness at design conditions; setting sensible AND latent effectiveness to 0.50 at every rating point gives enthalpy effectiveness exactly 0.50 by identity (both components of delta-h transfer at 50%) — minimum-compliant for the reference
energy_recovery.overshoot_article: 5.2.10.1.(6) — supply-air outlet temperature control + OutdoorAirPretreat setpoint manager are the required bypass/control against setpoint overshoot

water_economizer.text: 5.2.2.9.(1): HVAC systems that reduce mechanical cooling energy use by using outdoor air to chill cooling distribution fluid by direct evaporation, indirect evaporation, or both, shall be capable of cooling supply air so as to provide 100% of the cooling load when the outdoor air wet-bulb temperature is 7 C or lower. (2): the same, by sensible heat transfer, when the outdoor-air dry-bulb temperature is 10 C or lower.
water_economizer.modeling_note: Table -12 routes reference systems 2 and 5 to 5.2.2.9. Their Table 8.4.4.7.-B row prescribes a WATER-COOLED chiller, so the reference plant rejects heat through an evaporative cooling tower and the economizer chills the chilled water by INDIRECT EVAPORATION - sentence (1), the wet-bulb criterion, is the one that binds; sentence (2) would bind a dry-cooler arrangement the reference never builds. Built as a HeatExchangerFluidToFluid with the condenser loop as source and the chilled-water loop as load, UA and both design flows AUTOSIZED at sizing factor 1.0 so the exchanger is sized for the loop's full design cooling load (the modelled form of 'capable of 100% of the cooling load'), CoolingSetpointModulated onto a setpoint equal to the loop's own design exit temperature. The condenser setpoint is ALSO reset to follow the outdoor wet-bulb plus the tower's design approach (floored at the chilled-water setpoint, capped at the condenser design exit temperature): without that reset the tower stays pinned at 29 C, never delivers water colder than the chilled-water return, and the economizer is inert. control_type was chosen on measured evidence, not preference - see D-56.

humidification.text: Where present, humidification systems in the reference building shall use the same energy source as the corresponding humidification system in the proposed building.
humidification.modeling_note: The proposed's humidification is recorded per thermal block BEFORE the teardown that removes the proposed air loops, then rebuilt on the serving reference loop as the same EnergyPlus humidifier class (Humidifier:Steam:Electric -> electricity, Humidifier:Steam:Gas -> natural gas), capacity AUTOSIZED so the reference sizing run and the capacity iteration still govern it. Control is taken from the proposed, never invented: preferably the ZoneControlHumidistat that survives on the thermal zone, otherwise the proposed loop's own scheduled minimum-humidity-ratio setpoint. Where neither exists the humidifier is NOT built, because an uncontrolled humidifier never operates in EnergyPlus and would misrepresent the reference as humidified.

article_coverage.note: Complete accounting of Subsection 8.4.4 articles and how this gem handles each - emitted into every reference_hvac audit so nothing is silently missed. Statuses: implemented / partial / not_implemented / satisfied_by_clone / host_scope.

articles.title: General — reference building basis (prescriptive components, all energy uses)
articles.how: Whole-building modeling basis; the HVAC slice is governed by the articles below. Envelope/lighting/SHW conformance is composed by the umbrella from the sibling domain gems.

articles.title: Operating Schedules, Internal Loads and Service Water Heating Loads
articles.how: The reference model is a clone of the proposed model: schedules and internal/SHW loads remain identical, as required.

articles.title: Building Envelope Components (solar absorptance)
articles.how: Delegated to openstudio-envelope — reference_envelope applies this when composed by the umbrella.

articles.title: Envelope Thermal Characteristics (lightweight construction)
articles.how: Delegated to openstudio-envelope — reference_envelope applies this when composed by the umbrella.

articles.title: Lighting
articles.how: Delegated to openstudio-lighting — reference_lighting sets Part 4 allowance LPDs; reference_daylighting (ON by default, D-51; placement per the 4.2.2.1.(10)-(15) rule, D-57) covers sentences (5)-(12).

articles.title: Purchased Energy
articles.how: Purchased HEATING is represented by a gas-fired boiler (energy type = gas, sentence (1)(a)); purchased COOLING forces an air-cooled electric chiller (sentence (2)(a)) via the chw_source config.
articles.gaps: Capacity-ratio clauses (1)(b)/(2)(b) are sizing-time and not enforced; purchased SHW (3) is host-scope.

articles.title: HVAC System Selection (Tables -A/-B)
articles.how: Category election per Table -A (space type + storeys + cooling-kW threshold), closest-type fallback per sentence (3), residential special rules (D-34: heat-pump blocks take the sentence-(4) ASHP redirect before the compatible-cooling copy; water-loop HPs fall back to the Table -A rules per D-37), HP redirect per sentence (4), and the D-39 System 5 conditional (Table -B heating 'None' honoured for cooled-but-unheated blocks; 8.4.4.1.(5) presence override keeps the changeover heating when the proposed block heats).
articles.gaps: Sentence (2) 10%-area exclusion is a modeling choice left to the host. Table -B note (3) IS applied since D-28 (same-catalog multizone selection groups merge into whole-building systems; facade/internal/underground split inside the builder). Table -B note (1) humidification IS rebuilt since D-55 (the proposed's humidifier is recorded per thermal block before the teardown and re-created on the serving reference loop with the same energy source, autosized, and with a control taken from the proposed); mixed-category zone groups warn per (1) (T9); keyword-order category election can misfile compound names — museum exhibition areas land in Assembly via 'exhibit' (A6, awaiting adjudication).

articles.title: Equipment Oversizing
articles.how: Heating/cooling sizing factors set to min(proposed, 1.30/1.10) with the arithmetic recorded.

articles.title: Heating System
articles.how: System per Table -A (1); purchased energy (2); energy type follows proposed (4); boiler plant staging 176/352 kW incl. modulating flow mode + 25% floor and HWST 82/60 reset conventions applied via plant defaults + efficiency pass (6). Furnace staging (7) IS modelled since D-46: gas-heated reference systems 3/4 build as an AirLoopHVACUnitarySystem holding a multi-stage gas coil (the Table -13 ASHP holds multispeed DX coils on the same machinery), and a post-sizing pass sets the stage COUNT from the sized capacity (two equal stages at or below the threshold, ceil(kW / stage size) above it) with every stage capacity left AUTOSIZED - the equal increments come from the unitary's multispeed flow ratios, so capacity auto-iteration still works. Terminal/secondary split (3) accounted for systems 1/2/5 via Sizing:Zone dedicated-outdoor-air accounting with a neutral supply-air strategy (D-50): the terminal is sized on the space load alone and the make-up-air unit carries ventilation at system level.
articles.gaps: Multi-energy capacity ratios (5) are not modelled. (7): electric-resistance heating is not a furnace so it is not staged (D-49), zone-terminal and make-up-air DX/furnace equipment stays single-stage (D-48), and a system needing more than four equal stages is CLAMPED at four with a shouted audit warning because EnergyPlus multispeed objects cannot hold a fifth stage (D-47). (3): systems 3, 4 and 6 mix outdoor air into the supply stream, so their split is only approximated by ordinary mixed-air zone sizing with baseboards taking the residual - audited as an approximation, not claimed.

articles.title: Cooling Systems
articles.how: System per Table -A (1); purchased energy (2); energy type follows proposed (3); chiller plant: 2100 kW split, 7 C CHWST, 25% modulating floor (6) via plant defaults + efficiency pass. DX staging (8) IS modelled since D-46 on the same machinery as the furnace staging of the heating article: multispeed DX cooling inside an AirLoopHVACUnitarySystem on reference systems 3/4 and the ASHP, stage COUNT set post-sizing from the sized total, stage capacities AUTOSIZED, efficiencies and curves binned by the TOP-stage (= total) capacity and applied to every stage. Terminal/secondary split (7) accounted for systems 1/2/5 via Sizing:Zone dedicated-outdoor-air accounting (D-50).
articles.gaps: Multi-energy capacity ratios (4) are not modelled. (8): zone-terminal DX (packaged terminal units cannot host a multispeed coil in EnergyPlus) and make-up-air tempering DX stay single-speed (D-48), and stage counts above four are CLAMPED at the EnergyPlus ceiling with a shouted warning (D-47). (7): systems 3, 4 and 6 have no separate ventilation stream, so their split is approximated by mixed-air zone sizing and audited as such.

articles.title: Cooling Tower Systems
articles.how: Tower cell count (1750 kW rule) and fan power set from chiller heat rejection in the efficiency pass. Tower design temps 35/29 C water, 24 C wb ARE set by the builder; cells per (2)-(3) with true ceiling; fan at the Table 5.2.12.2 0.013 kW/kW maximum.
articles.gaps: Fan cycling to the 29 C setpoint relies on CoolingTowerSingleSpeed default capacity control; pump is variable-speed hardware modeled with constant-power coefficients pending the constant-speed pump ruling (T-list).

articles.title: Cooling with Outside Air (economizers)
articles.gaps: DX staging clauses 5.2.2.8.(4)-(5) are not enforced. The 5.2.2.9 capability is realized as an INTEGRATED economizer against the prescribed 7 C chilled-water setpoint: measured hour by hour it carries 100% of the chilled-water load in every hour at outdoor wet-bulb 7 C or lower (the sentence-(1) criterion), and a partial share above that band; systems whose chilled water is air-cooled or purchased have no evaporatively-cooled fluid to economize with and are warned instead.
articles.how: air economizers (Table -12 -> 5.2.2.8) applied to reference systems 1/3/4/6 + HP with mechanical cooling: DifferentialEnthalpy control, up to 100% OA. Systems 2/5 get the 5.2.2.9 WATER-side economizer since D-56: a HeatExchangerFluidToFluid between the condenser and chilled-water loops, UA and both design flows autosized at sizing factor 1.0 (sized for the loop's full design cooling load), CoolingSetpointModulated onto the loop design exit temperature, plus the condenser setpoint reset to the outdoor wet-bulb + tower approach without which the tower stays at 29 C and the economizer is inert. Sentence (1) (wet-bulb 7 C) binds because the reference rejects heat evaporatively; (2) is declared inapplicable rather than ignored.

articles.title: Heat Pumps
articles.how: D-37 (Note A-8.4.4.13, retrieved via MCP): the printed split — water-LOOP heat pumps (internal loop, aux boiler/tower allowed) KEEP their Table -A selection per sentence (1); air-, water- and ground-SOURCE heat pumps redirect to the Table -13 packaged rooftop ASHP per sentence (2), with the source classified from the HP's source plant loop (ground HX / district / temperature-source => external) and no-evidence detections keeping the conservative redirect; -10 C heating cutoff applied (2)(d). (2)(b) cooling-peak sizing without oversizing holds by measurement (per-zone factor 1.0 overrides the capped global; D-52); (2)(c) heating=cooling identity via align_heat_pump_heating_capacity (D-22); (2)(g) the 33% auxiliary-fuel election runs on the proposed building's ANNUAL delivered-heat data (the proposed annual is run before the reference build), aggregated per (g)(i)/(g)(ii) scope, falling back to the structural 8.4.4.9.(4) proxy — audited either way (D-52).
articles.gaps: (2)(c)'s -8.3 C point evaluates to 47.8% on the vendored legacy CAP_FT curve against the code's 50% (known approximation, D-52 review). The (2)(g) election needs annual data: simulate: :sizing/:none runs keep the structural proxy, audited as such.

articles.title: Hydronic Pumps
articles.how: Table 8.4.4.14. riding-curve coefficients + below-D minimum-flow clamp on every reference PumpVariableSpeed ((4)-(5)), applied POST-SIZING by the efficiency pass; proposed combined peak W/(L/s) per plant-loop type transferred to reference pump rated power ((1)-(3), needs the sized proposed via apply_efficiencies proposed:) — unknown proposed pumps or unsized flows warn loudly. D-38: the transferred power is then clamped min-wins at the Table 5.2.6.3 combined-pump maximum (W per kW of loop peak thermal demand; 8.4.4.1.(2) makes Part 5 a ceiling for the reference).
articles.gaps: (6) 5.2.12.1 pump-energy-inclusive secondary-system adjustment is not implemented; (2)'s combined peak transfers as W/(L/s) INTENSITY (x reference flow), not absolute watts — reference flows legitimately differ from proposed.

articles.title: Outdoor Air
articles.how: Spaces (and their DesignSpecificationOutdoorAir) are retained by the clone; rebuilt systems draw the same peak OA specifications (1). DCV strategies (2) ARE copied since D-54: each proposed air loop's Controller:MechanicalVentilation demand-controlled-ventilation flag and system outdoor-air method are recorded per thermal block by the characterization (before the teardown that removes the proposed loop) and re-applied to the rebuilt reference controller, the method only when it is itself a demand-control method (IndoorAirQualityProcedure* / ProportionalControl*).
articles.gaps: OA identity (1) holds only for DSOA-driven proposeds — hard-set proposed minimum-OA controller values draw a runtime warning (T7). (2): the peak-rate outdoor-air methods (ZoneSum, Standard 62.1 Ventilation Rate Procedure) are deliberately NOT copied because they determine the peak rate that sentence (1) governs; where a reference system merges thermal blocks of which only some carry DCV, the single reference controller applies the strategy to all of them and says so in a warning.

articles.title: Space Temperature Control (radiant workaround, throttling range)
articles.gaps: (1)'s +-2 C radiant workaround applies ONLY when the tool cannot model radiant effects — EnergyPlus can (ZoneHVAC low-temperature radiant objects); it binds only if the modeller chooses to approximate a radiant proposed design convectively, and applying the adjustment is then the modeller's responsibility.
articles.how: (2) throttling range is identical by construction: both buildings use ideal thermostat control on cloned schedules (8.4.3.2) — there is no throttling knob that could differ.

articles.title: Fans (exhaust fans, fan power vs flow curves)
articles.how: VAV fan power-vs-flow curves from Table -17 applied in the (post-sizing) efficiency pass, row selected by rated power per sentences (3)-(5); the below-D floor is approximated by the E+ minimum-flow-fraction clamp (equals E within table rounding)

articles.title: Supply Air Systems (airflow rates, fan specs)
articles.how: Fan specs applied: systems 1-5 supply 640 Pa @ 40% with no return-fan spec; system 6 supply 1000 Pa @ 55% + return 250 Pa @ 30% ((3)-(4)); system 6 13 C SAT via the catalog sizing block.
articles.gaps: Supply-airflow determination at 21/11 C deltas ((1)-(2)) is sizing-time; sentences (5)-(6) (identical fan power / 5.2.12.1-included fan energy) are not modeled.

articles.title: Energy Recovery Systems
articles.how: Table 5.2.10.1.-A/-B airflow-threshold trigger (climate row by HDD x %OA band x continuous/non-continuous from the air loop availability schedule, >=8000 h/yr) evaluated POST-SIZING per reference air loop on sized supply/OA flows; rotary HX @ 50% effectiveness with OA-pretreat control added where required. Below-10%-OA systems are outside the Tables (NR).
articles.gaps: Ice-plant heat-recovery rules (3) are not modeled (no ice plants in scope). Reference fans default to Always On from the topology builders, classifying most systems CONTINUOUS (Table -B: R at >=10% OA for HDD >= 3000) — wiring reference fan availability to the archetype operating schedule would flip many to non-continuous; open item, every determination audits its inputs.

articles.title: Service Water Heating Systems
articles.how: Delegated to openstudio-shw — reference_shw re-applies Part 6 minimum efficiencies.

articles.title: General — HVAC components accounted
articles.how: HVAC components accounted per the prescriptive Section 5.2 requirements via the reference system builds (8.4.4.7.-8.4.4.19.) and the capacity-binned efficiency pass — the realization of 8.4.1.1.(1) for the HVAC slice.

articles.title: HVAC Systems
articles.how: Reference HVAC systems are built explicitly from the Table 8.4.4.7. topologies — components are constructed, not approximated by thermodynamically-similar substitutes.
articles.gaps: (2) limited-capability effects (terminal/primary/secondary interactions) are EnergyPlus behaviour of the built systems, not separately verified.
